children: Hungary's seasonally-adjusted Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) edged down to 51.3 in August (HUPMI=ECI) from 51.4 in July, the index publisher said on Tuesday.

The August figure fell short of a long-term monthly average of 52.7 but was higher than an average 49.7 August reading in the past three years, the Association of Logistics, Purchasing and Inventory Management said.
"Survey respondents in August reported a slower expansion of the manufacturing industry compared with the previous month," the index publisher said in a statement.
The index of new orders was lower but still showed expansion. The production volume index fell from the previous month and shows an expansion.
The 50-point mark separates contraction from growth.
The index for purchase prices was lower and continued to show an intense rise in prices, the publisher said.
The employment index edged down but still showed expansion. The export and import indicators were both lower but showed expansion.
